data.narrative:
Quantum Motion is a Series C quantum computing company founded by John Morton and Simon Benjamin, having raised $160M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 tracked peers—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private, including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Given the nascent stage and technical heterogeneity of quantum computing, a narrow peer-median approach is not reliable; only 0 same-stage and 0 adjacent-stage comparables meet sufficient data density thresholds. Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression analysis, which applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $160M total-raised proxy. This method implies a valuation of $272M. Sensitivity around this point yields a low-end estimate of $231M (applying conservative step-up assumptions) and a high-end of $313M (applying more aggressive progression).

The valuation range of $231M–$313M, with a median of $272M, reflects the single applicable triangulation method and should be treated as directional. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent comparable transactions at similar stage and the rapid pace of technical progress and consolidation in quantum computing, which may shift relative positioning materially. Any upward pressure on valuation would require disclosure of material technical milestones, customer commitments, or narrowing of the competitive landscape.
